sense: every one of, the whole number of

terms.grammar: adjective, third declension; in the plural, all (people, things)
evidence: Verg. Ecl. 8.63: nōn omnia possumus omnēs
terms.comment: In the plural, “all”: omnēs, all (people), omnia, all (things) (see everyone, everything). In the singular it is “every” (see every), or all of a kind or a mass: omne forum, all the square (Prud. Perist. 3.177). For all of one thing taken whole, Latin prefers tōtus.
One thing, all of it: tōta domus, all the house; with a word of time, “all … long”: tōtum diem (see whole).
Lewis & Short: from conjūnctus, “all in a body, all together”, the members thought of as joined.

evidence: Tac. Agr. 12.2: ita singulī pugnant, ūniversī vincuntur
terms.comment: All at once, as one body, as against singulī, one by one.

phrases.english: to order all the men to have their meal
I serve the same to all

phrases.latin: ecce nivem glaciālis hiems ingerit et tegit omne forum
phrases.english: look, icy winter is heaping up snow and covering all the square
so they fight one at a time and are beaten all together
